description: Figures how much of a household's 2026 or 2027 (tax_year) Social Security benefits is taxable, the federal income tax and the part of it the benefits cost, the effective marginal rate on the next dollar of other income, how many cents of benefits each extra dollar makes taxable, and which part of the torpedo the household is in. Computed by QuantCalc's federal tax API, as the website's tax torpedo calculator; requires a connected QuantCalc PRO licence or Tax Season Pass, and without one returns no figures and names the free page. Not tax advice.

age.description: The age reached in the tax year (18-110): the age-65 deductions depend on it.

filing_status.description: Filing status: single, married filing jointly (mfj), married filing separately (mfs) or head of household (hoh).

investment_income.description: Other investment income (interest, dividends), taxed as ordinary income here, as on the free page. Default 0.

social_security.description: Gross Social Security benefits of the household.

spouse_age.description: Joint return only: the spouse's age reached in the tax year. Default the same as age, stated.

tax_exempt_interest.description: Tax-exempt interest: not taxed, but it counts in provisional income. Default 0.

tax_year.description: The tax year: 2026 (default) or 2027 (the IRS's published 2027 amounts, Rev. Proc. 2026-35; the benefit thresholds are fixed by law). Stated in the result.

name: social_security_taxable_amount
title: Taxable Social Security and the tax torpedo rate
